claim.quote: A blind analysis of nuclear recoil events with energies between 3.3 keV and 60.5 keV finds no significant excess. This leads to a minimum upper limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section of 2.58e-47 cm^2 for a WIMP mass of 28 GeV/c^2 at 90% confidence level.

name: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment

summary.plain: XENONnT looked for dark matter particles bumping into xenon nuclei for the first time. It saw nothing beyond ordinary background, which let it rule out a wide range of possible dark matter particles more tightly than any liquid-xenon experiment before it.
summary.technical: 1.1 tonne-year exposure, 5.9 t sensitive mass, blind analysis of nuclear recoils between 3.3 and 60.5 keV. No significant excess; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross section excluded above 2.58e-47 cm^2 at 28 GeV/c^2 (90% CL), improving on XENON1T for the same exposure.

title: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment
why_it_matters: XENONnT's first WIMP search already improved on XENON1T's limits for the same exposure, demonstrating the upgraded detector's lower background and larger target mass.
